findings.text: the landing record says a pass-through reading of the pointer made test_still_working_disposition_expires_when_the_run_turns_terminal fail and that the narrowed reading is what keeps the head arm from adding a failing id, but no log in the run directory carries that id (grep over the run's *.log, including gate-baseline-first.log and gate-pre-existing.log, returns nothing) — its only receipt is the run's own transcript stream.jsonl — while every neighbouring claim in the same record names a log beside it, so the reader checking why the drain carries only a proven answer has to open a 12 MB transcript rather than the log the record points at.

the tests field offers the arm command with both trees substituted as <tree>, so the one line a reader lands on first cannot reproduce either arm's invocation; the two exact commands exist only inside the baseline_suite and after_suite JSON. The counts on that line are accurate against the logs (261 collected in both arms, 19 failed/242 passed at 68a5b96b, 17 failed/244 passed at 09e33ae5, no failing id added), so this is a record defect rather than a measurement one.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit — 713dbde8 routes the drain through the host gate, c84429e5 narrows the carried answer to a proven-only reading, 09e33ae5 joins the repair's new lines to the form the declared formatter produces, and 09feaea7/e629466b/0fb5709a carry the landing record and the figure — all inside the declared write paths.
item_verdicts.done_when: the followup's three cases exist at tests/test_a_foreign_pid_never_reads_dead.py (the foreign row with a local number, the foreign pointer with an exit record, and the control launched here with an absent pid); the first two fail at 68a5b96b on assert True is not True (gate-baseline.log, and the borrowed life is the row's own process_alive True) and assert None is not None at row["exit_record"] is not None, with the identical test-file digest 73fa97e67fd54a33a68758c4fe2ce8885a9bd5e4f54e1f727e2f4fdfb0bbbc03 in both arms; the control passes in both arms; and the head arm's failing set is a strict subset of the baseline's (19 to 17).
item_verdicts.goal: the drain now asks the host-gated reading its sibling views use: reckon/crew/runs.py:1036 takes alive, proven = local_liveness(pointer) and passes process_alive: alive if proven else None into classify_pointer, so a run launched on another host whose pid number this host happens to hold no longer reads alive (null, unproven) and a foreign run whose supervisor exit record is on disk reads process gone through the record instead of being suppressed by a borrowed live answer.
item_verdicts.manifest: read at sha256 d292c170d961f2fc74c06312edf2f425c15acf3658793e38d4f6495e7725f98d; status complete, six commits, both arms as armed JSON keyed to their revisions with log paths and complete id lists (19 and 17), measurement_module/measurement_cwd naming the scratch tree's imported module, and a negative-control log named as a bare path whose first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim, and the run's own check-manifest reports ok: true — but the tests field templates both trees as <tree> (FINDING at manifest.md:14), and the file moved under this review: the state first read carried an unsubstituted placeholder path in after_suite.command and one id of the nineteen its own failure_count stated, repaired in place at 10:48.
item_verdicts.write_paths: git diff --stat 68a5b96b..0fb5709a lists exactly the four declared paths — reckon/crew/runs.py, docs/evidence/fragments/a-stalled-row-says-whether-the-worker-lives/drain-view-reads-the-host-gated-liveness.html, the figure under docs/figures/a-stalled-row-says-whether-the-worker-lives/drain-view-reads-the-host-gated-liveness/, and tests/test_a_foreign_pid_never_reads_dead.py — 360 insertions and 15 deletions, and the worktree is clean at head.

justifications.durability: the cases discriminate rather than merely pass: two red at the base revision under the same test bytes and green at head, with a third that differs in one fact and is green in both, the real ~/.config/reckon fingerprinted around every case, and the declared mutation shown to remove the repair's discrimination rather than breaking the fixture — one point off because two cases assert the word through recovery._process_reading, a private helper, so a rename or a recomposition there would redline the test without a behaviour change.
justifications.evidence: exemplary in the main: one log per arm with a header naming revision, tree, command, resolved working directory, imported module path and the tested file's digest, repeats kept beside the fence, a negative control whose first line carries the declared mutation and whose tail carries EXIT=1, and a ruff delta measured inside each arm's own tree; two findings deduct — a load-bearing claim in the landing record whose receipt is only the run transcript, and a top-level tests field that templates both trees.
justifications.fit: the drain consumes the same narrowed reading as the sibling views instead of a second rule, the new comments state the mechanism and the borrowed-life reason with no plan, stage, node or ticket name, test names state behaviour, and the repair's own formatting join is its own commit rather than folded into the repair.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the repair is one call site in the view the followup named, it reuses the helper the sibling repair introduced rather than adding a second reading (local_liveness is now called from reckon/crew/runs.py:1036 beside reckon/sprint_liveness.py:153 and reckon/crew/recovery.py:3925), and both directions the followup asks for are measured: the borrowed life is refused and the recorded end is read.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff against the declared base is exactly the four declared paths at 360 insertions and 15 deletions, no other path appears in any of the six commits, and the worktree carries no untracked or uncommitted work.
